thread:
maria: Quick question — if we let tenants edit SLO thresholds in the console, how do we ensure the CLI/infra-configured sampling & routing policies fold back correctly? e.g. if tenant lowers p99 threshold locally, we don't want it to bypass global quota/fanout rules.
ryan: Good call. My read: console edits should be surface-only and produce a delta that goes through the same policy-enforcer API. Don't let the console mutate the routing policy store directly. :+1:
akash: We also need telemetry parity. If console edits change sampling, our telemetry should tag samples with origin=console vs origin=api so rollouts/alerts don't get noisy.
nina: Can we enforce a nonoverride mode? Console exposes sliders but they POST to a validation endpoint that either maps -> policy change (allowed) or -> suggested override (not applied).
josh: +1 to validation endpoint. Also need a contract for reversion: if global policy changes upstream, console-saved deltas should be auto-reconciled or expire.
deploy-bot: Deployment started: policy-enforcer v2 -> canary 10% (sha: a1b2c3) — monitor slo-alerting-service latency.
maria: Example flow I sketched earlier: console PATCH -> /v1/policies/deltas -> policy-enforcer validates against tenant-quota and routing-compat -> emits effect (allowed|suggested|rejected). If allowed, effect stored as delta with ttl.
akash: Right. Also add sample annotation in logs: {"tenant_id":"t-123","mod_origin":"console","delta_id":"d-456"}
sam: UX nit: we should show a warning banner in the console when their change will increase fanout or could poke an escalation path. Otherwise product teams will flip sliders blindly.
nina: Agree. Also add an audit row in the tenant timeline and a link "View resulting routing policy" that opens a diff against global policy.
ryan: Implementation detail: policy-enforcer should return a normalized policy fingerprint so console can cache & show "matches current deployment" vs "pending reconciliation".
josh: We need to decide TTL semantics: suggested deltas -> 24h auto-expire? allowed deltas -> persistent until explicit revoke or global conflict. Thoughts?
maria: For rollout safety, allowed deltas should be soft until aligned with a rate-limiter check. Maybe: allowed + soft=true => apply with sampled ramp 1% -> 10% -> 100% over 6 hours. That prevents blast.
akash: API payload sketch:
```
PATCH /v1/policies/deltas
{
  "tenant_id":"t-123",
  "changes": [{"route":"/embed","p99_ms":500}],
  "origin":"console",
  "ttl_secs":86400
}
```
response 200 {"delta_id":"d-456","action":"accepted","ramp_policy":"soft-6h-1-100"}

sam: Can we log a telemetry metric: delta_applied{origin, tenant, route, ramp_policy}? That will help detect noisy tenants and surface for ops.
ryan: +1. Also we should increment an alert counter if delta causes a simulated fanout > threshold during validation. validation should run a "what-if" fanout calc.
josh: Edge: what about CLI users who manage infra-as-code? They will want deltas as commitable artifacts. Maybe we expose deltas as resources that can be fetched and committed back into infra repo.
maria: Good idea — expose GET /v1/policies/deltas?tenant=t-123 to list, and include a field "applied=false|true|pending" so infra tooling can pick up.
nina: Final UX ask: add a small lock icon and text "Managed by infra (CLI)" when a policy delta originated from infra git, making console edits read-only for those keys.
maria: OK actionable checklist:
- console -> PATCH -> validation endpoint (policy-enforcer) (maria/ryan)
- annotate telemetry with origin and delta_id (akash)
- implement soft-ramp semantics and TTL (josh)
- show warning banner & diff link in console (nina/sam)
- expose deltas as resources for infra -> GET/commit (ryan/josh)
I'll open a tiny RFC and wire some tests for the fanout simulator.
sam: :thumbsup: 
nina: Thanks — will mock the UX banners this afternoon.
